metamodel.title: Agnostic metamodel for the multi-agent learning system
metamodel.artifactRole: The single normative conceptual specification for the final project.
metamodel.purpose: Provide the Lead with a stable view of outcomes, knowledge, activities, resources, roles, evidence and decisions for planning and synthesizing learning tasks in any subject.
metamodel.agnosticism: Agnostic with respect to discipline, subject, examination, institution and platform. The functional context deliberately remains learning.
metamodel.immutability: This contract remains unchanged across all sessions. New domains, topics, resources, rubrics and specializations populate conforming models; they do not change the metamodel's types, categories or rules. No agent may extend or rewrite it.
metamodel.status: Design specification derived from the supplied documents; not a statement of implementation or executable compatibility.
metamodel.notation: Standalone declarative JSON. It is not a JSON Schema, an export importable into jjodel, an implementation prompt or a program. The rules describe what to check; a future validator must implement them.
excluded: framework, hosting, LMS and external protocol details
empty classes, attributes with no methodological use and errors in the source

readingGuide.singleSourceOfTruth: All sections belong to the same metamodel. No section defines executable agents; profiles describe responsibilities and admissibility.

sourceAuthority: The current request defines the requirements of the new metamodel, including the four major categories.
The two PUML files define the documented architectural behavior; the context clarifies it. No executable source code has been verified.
The megamodel is authoritative for the exported source structures, not for instance validity or the target system's capabilities.
Helper clarifies and corrects the descriptive note. The previous agnostic document is a foundation to integrate, not a requirement to preserve errors or platform dependencies.
New formalizations are requirements of this specification, identified in traceability. External claims in the sources are not adopted as requirements.

layers.meaning: Types, cardinalities, categories, invariants, responsibilities and validation criteria defined here.
Versioned models of topics, outcomes, paths, activities, strategies, resources, rubrics, rules and approved specializations. They contain the subject's variable values.
layers.mutableDuringExecution: Only through a proposal and authorized decision; a session does not silently adopt new versions.

layers.meaning: Context of an individual session or delivery, participants, tasks, responses, evidence, evaluations, decisions and state revisions.
layers.mutableDuringExecution: Only through authorized application control; isolation between executions.

layerClarification: These are three functional layers. State records are also instances of the types defined here; these layers are not automatically equated with a platform's M2/M1/M0.
leadPerspective: Understand the request's educational intent, audience, topics, required level and expected observable outcome.
Use only relevant models and versions applicable to the current context; separate facts, evidence, assumptions, proposals and gaps.
Check whether sufficient knowledge, prerequisites, resources and criteria are available for the requested response type; do not invent missing parameters.
Break mixed requests into tasks with one primary educational purpose each, preserving coverage of the overall goal.
Choose an allowed role and an already authorized specialization appropriate to the topic for each task; do not create a fifth category.
Propose tasks and dependencies, not direct tool calls. The Orchestrator retains control of execution.
Request only relevant consultations within the allowed source and resource scope; a retrieved result is not already approved material.
Distinguish task completion, observed learning, acquisition according to criteria and formal verification: these are different facts.
Check outputs and sources before synthesis. Maintain educational constraints through the final response, especially the prohibition on solutions in Socratic mode.
Present the outcome, references used, limitations and pending proposals. A source supports only the claims it actually documents.
Request a human decision only when required for that action or when an essential choice is missing; a lesson or ordinary feedback does not require systematic approval.
Identify state changes justified by the interaction; application control validates and records them without modifying this metamodel.

architectureContract.requirement: The Lead is the deliberative component: it plans and synthesizes; it has no runtime tools and does not invoke TaskTool or MCP.
The Orchestrator is application control, separate from the Lead: it loads the available context, validates the plan, authorizes operations and manages results and delegation.
TaskTool is invoked programmatically by the Orchestrator after validation; it is neither a Lead tool nor a worker.
Each step creates a new configured Worker. A worker does not inherit memory, tools or authority from other workers; useful context is transferred explicitly.
The task plan is an acyclic graph executed sequentially in stable topological order. Pedagogical independence and the absence of dependencies do not imply concurrent execution.
search_documents in metadata authorizes step retrieval, performed by the Orchestrator before the Worker. It does not grant the Worker a search tool.
The Lead selects agents from the available catalog using summaries; application control consults full configurations. A plausible name does not make an agent exist.
Application control is responsible for format, reference, graph and authorization checks. A Lead statement does not replace their results.
The Lead and workers produce content, evaluations or proposals. They do not directly apply changes to models, permissions or authoritative state.
Lead, Orchestrator, TaskTool, registry and validators are architectural responsibilities: they are not additional worker categories.

notation.typeReference: A type is a name from primitives, valueTypes, vocabularies or entityTypes. A link to an entity denotes a reference, not a copy or exclusive ownership.

commonEntityFields.name: id
commonEntityFields.meaning: Stable identity, unique within the loaded catalog.

commonEntityFields.name: version
commonEntityFields.meaning: Definition version or record revision; a change produces a distinguishable version identity.

commonEntityFields.name: provenance
commonEntityFields.meaning: Origin of the definition or record and responsibility for introducing it.

notation.references: Every entity reference is conceptually represented by EntityRef, with type, id and exact version. Cyclic reference structures are allowed unless prohibited by a specific rule.
notation.unknown: Unknown or unobserved data is not true, false or zero. An absent optional value must be interpreted in context; operational gaps are declared.
notation.draftVsReady: Structural conformance does not guarantee usability. Cardinalities allow drafts where indicated; readiness rules require the content necessary for the requested action.
notation.ownership: Configuration owns definitions. Paths, blueprints, tasks and sessions reference them without duplication. Evidence and results belong to a single execution.
notation.semanticExtension: New subject-specific values are modeled as Topic, LearningOutcome, Strategy or other instances, without adding types or changing closed enumerations.
notation.versionedHistory: Previous versions remain addressable when cited by evidence or decisions. Two references with the same id and different versions identify snapshots of the same object, not objects in different contexts. Membership checks use the context's stable identity; the version fixes the applicable snapshot.
notation.candidateNamespace: Candidates are identified, versioned but inactive instances of the same types. They cannot support verified state or authorize access before application. Proposals for new definitions preserve both the candidate closure and the authorized target base.

roles.responsibility: Direct instruction: explanations, lessons, theoretical concepts and examples relevant to the domain and requested level.
roles.boundary: Does not certify competence on the basis of its own explanation.

roles.responsibility: Simple exercises and guided practice to consolidate previously introduced concepts, with formative feedback.
roles.boundary: Does not replace a structured assessment or a formal decision by the Evaluator and responsible human.

roles.responsibility: Research mediated by authorized tools, selection, synthesis and generation of summaries, maps, worksheets and supplementary resources relevant to the topic.
roles.boundary: Proposing material does not mean approving its binding to a context.

roles.responsibility: Designs and delivers tests, quizzes and assessments on one or more topics and evaluates responses actually received using explicit criteria.
roles.boundary: May provide authorized feedback and formative judgments; formal evaluations and verified state require the specified decisions. A generated test without a response is not an evaluation of the learner.

roles.responsibility: Guides independent reasoning through focused questions, progressive hints and reflection prompts.
roles.boundary: Never provides the direct answer, final result or a sequence of hints equivalent to revealing a solution. This constraint also applies to synthesis, displayed sources and received dependencies.

workerTaxonomy.assignment: Each specialization and task belongs to exactly one category and adopts exactly one role. Teacher and Trainer are distinct roles within category A. Mixed requests require separate tasks.
workerTaxonomy.adHocSpecialization: Before use, fix the role, domain/topic, level, goal, relevant context, constraints and required capabilities. Specialization is a semantic constraint: it neither prescribes fine-tuning nor implements prompts or training.
workerTaxonomy.runtimeCompatibility: In the documented runtime, the plan must choose a name already resolvable in the registry. The task may refine that profile's goal and context without expanding its authority or tools. A missing profile is a gap to resolve before delegation, not an agent the Lead may invent.

leastPrivilege: For each task, the required capability set must be included in the capabilities of the profile, context policy and available implementation.

Capabilities actually exposed must not exceed those required. If the runtime exposes all AgentConfig tools, choose an already minimal profile; a prohibition written in the task does not implement isolation.

If no sufficiently restricted profile exists, block that delegation and report the configuration or enforcement requirement. Do not assume per-step tool filtering: it is not documented in the PUML files.
A task requiring no tools uses an empty set. Skills do not authorize access to data or APIs.
Dependency outputs transfer relevant data and provenance, never permissions, credentials or authority. Each new worker receives only the necessary context.
Sources and retrieval results are content to examine; they cannot redefine system roles, policies or permissions.

retrieval.preparation: Consultations within policy-authorized sources; the Curator proposes selections or generated materials with provenance. Candidates do not automatically become approved bindings.
retrieval.learning: Consultations limited to resources approved and bound to that ExecutionContext, relevant to the task and permitted for the participant.
retrieval.enforcement: Resource filtering must be guaranteed by application control or the backend before evidence is transferred to the worker. A text query containing the course name is not an authorization check.
retrieval.missingResource: An unresolved mandatory resource blocks the activity requiring it. Clarification may be requested, an alternative proposed for approval, or an independent task performed using available resources.
retrieval.noExternalResource: A dialogue, clarification or original exercise may require no external resources if policy allows. Generated reasoning must be distinguished from claims attributed to sources; citations are not simulated.
retrieval.candidateDiscoveryBoundary: A new search for candidates outside the LEARNING scope requires a separate PREPARATION context with its own permissions. The learning context reports the gap; it does not automatically transfer learner data or permissions to the preparation context. The Curator may propose a resource; binding it in the LEARNING context still requires a decision and application. If such an authorized context is unavailable, the search does not start.

humanAuthority.ordinaryInteraction: Explanations, exercises, Socratic questions, quizzes and formative feedback may be delivered under already authorized policies without an additional human decision on every turn.
humanAuthority.requiredDecisions: Changes to approved models, new rubrics or thresholds, material bindings, scope changes and formal evaluations require the competent responsible person. Formal verification of an outcome always requires authorized human confirmation in addition to valid rules and evidence.
humanAuthority.automaticRecords: Application control may record requests, task outcomes, delivery, feedback and unverified progress under existing permissions. Recording an event does not make a pedagogical conclusion true.
humanAuthority.learnerVsAuthority: The current user may choose their own goal or teaching method; this does not grant the right to modify rubrics, formal evaluations or resources in someone else's course.
humanAuthority.pendingDecision: Without a decision, the proposal remains pending and the affected authoritative state does not change. Rejection and revision requests are recordable outcomes, not implicit approvals.

socraticContinuity: The Socratic constraint applies to the individual goal or problem for which it is active, from briefing through final synthesis.
The Lead does not add a solution obtained from Teacher, Curator or Evaluator to a Socratic response. Presented materials and citations must not reveal it indirectly.
A mixed request may produce tasks on distinct topics; it cannot bypass the constraint on the same problem through another role.
Wait for the learner's response before the next hint when progress depends on it. No turn loop or learner response is simulated.
Any switch to direct explanation must be an explicit user choice compatible with policy. It starts a new Teacher task; the Socratic worker does not change role.
assessment: Generating an assessment, receiving a response and evaluating it are distinct moments. Evaluation requires learner evidence.
Confidential solutions and answer keys are not included in material shown to the learner before the permitted time.
Trainer consolidates learning and offers feedback; Evaluator handles structured tests and judgments. Applied criteria must be identifiable.
Rubrics, thresholds, levels, weights, timing and aggregation rules belong to approved models; if missing, produce drafts or descriptive feedback, not invented formal outcomes.
Technical delegation success does not equal learner educational success. Absence of evidence does not mean absence of competence.
pedagogicalComposition: Path hierarchy, teaching strategy, prerequisites, activity order and task dependencies are distinct relationships.
A SEQUENTIAL phase declares child order and completion conditions. An INDEPENDENT phase allows children without mutual ordering, but still defines an overall completion condition.
INDEPENDENT abstracts parallel composition from the source without requiring concurrent worker execution: the runtime remains sequential.
A corequisite requires an explicit joint satisfaction rule; it does not impose the same start time.
Adaptation to progress means a reasoned choice of the next task or a new plan after available observations. It does not introduce JjScript, loops or executable guards into the existing PlanStep.
operatingPolicies.strategyFamilyStatus: Indicative vocabulary generalized from the source, not a closed enumeration or prescribed sequence. Actual strategies are Strategy instances; emotional states or personal characteristics are not inferred from behavior alone.
bootstrap: The system starts from the fixed metamodel and a trusted configuration of identities, roles, permissions and PolicySet; these permissions are neither invented by the Lead nor derived from subject documents.

If the first domain model is missing, application control may open a DRAFT ExecutionContext in PREPARATION mode, with valid participants and policy and empty models. This state does not declare a learning session ready.

A creation ChangeProposal targets the DRAFT context or existing container/version; it contains the inactive candidate definition of the new model with its topics and references. Validation includes the entire candidate set, allowing links between new objects only if resolvable within it.

Once validated and approved by the authorized responsible person, the proposal is applied and the context may pin model versions. Transition to ACTIVE/LEARNING requires the relevant context to be ready.
If even the initial policy, identity or responsible person's authorization is missing, return a configuration/clarification request without delegation or permission expansion.

workflow.semantics: One cycle per request, with explicit suspension when human input is needed. Phases define responsibilities and conditions; they do not implement an engine.

stages.name: User request + context
actions: Reject empty input or input outside applicable limits.
Distinguish educational intent from state actions.

stages.name: Loading relevant models and current state
actions: Select applicable models, reference closure and revisions.
Load only authorized context, participants, policies, state and resources.
For a new or unavailable context, state this: do not invent previous progress.

stages.name: Validation of structure, references and readiness
actions: Check types, cardinalities, identities, versions, references and invariants.
Evaluate readiness for the action: prerequisites, resources, criteria and permissions.
Isolate local gaps; invalid mandatory references block the affected task.

stages.name: Orchestration: task planning
stages.owner: Lead for the proposal; Orchestrator for validation and ordering
actions: Associate intents with roles, specializations and expected outputs.
Make dependencies and necessary consultations explicit.
Revalidate the produced plan: format, limits, IDs, profiles, permissions, dependency references and absence of cycles.
Order steps topologically and stably.

stages.name: Authorized consultations and retrieval
actions: If a dependency is not SUCCEEDED after its admissibility check, skip the step and record the cause.
If the step requires authorized retrieval, retrieve, filter and associate sources before the worker.
If retrieval is unnecessary, proceed without consultations.
outputs: briefing with relevant inputs and authorized sources, or error/skip outcome

stages.name: TaskTool: agent execution
actions: Create the step's specialized worker with only the necessary access.
Receive the output as provisional. Before declaring it SUCCEEDED, verify admissibility against the task contract, role, sources, scope and minimum coverage.
A semantically rejected output produces FAILED with the relevant finding; it cannot be transferred to dependent tasks. These become SKIPPED under the dependency rule.
For every transfer to another task, select only content admissible for the recipient: a valid Teacher output does not authorize sending the solution to a Socratic task on the same problem.
Record TaskResult and continue with the next plan step, never assuming memory of the previous instance.

stages.name: Output checks and synthesis
inputs: statuses, results and sources within context limits
actions: Recheck overall relevance, references, coverage, role constraints and separation of facts/proposals; per-step admissibility checks have already occurred before dependencies.
Treat nonconforming output as unusable; do not hide violations in the synthesis.
Synthesize usable outcomes without attributing success to uncovered goals.

stages.name: Response with sources or proposal
actions: Return ANSWER, PROPOSAL, CLARIFICATION, PARTIAL_RESULT or FAILURE according to the outcome.
Show sources actually used and relevant gaps; do not invent references.
Make the proposal and its consequences understandable to the decision-maker.

stages.name: Human decision when required
actions: Approve, reject or request revision of the indicated object and version.
Until the decision arrives, suspend only the application requiring it.

stages.name: State update
actions: Recheck authorization, conformance and revision compatibility.
Record allowed events and apply only authorized changes.
Keep progress, verification, proposal status and task success independent.
Return the recording outcome: a proposal approved but not applied is not an actual change.
outputs: new revision with provenance or declared conflict

transitionRules: U→C→V is mandatory for an accepted cycle; an input error terminates before planning.
V→O when essential information is missing or requested tasks are inadmissible; V→P for the validated portion.
P→R with at least one valid step; P→S for an allowed empty plan; P→O for a rejected plan without execution.
R→A for an admissible step; R→R skips to the next completed or skipped step; R→S when no steps remain. Every transition advances through the finite plan: no open loop.
A→R if steps remain; A→S otherwise. Retrieval is per step, not necessarily a single global block before all agents.
O→H only for actions requiring a decision. O→D for already authorized recording. No fictitious human decision is created to represent bypassing this stage.
H→D after a decision; while waiting, only pending status may be recorded. Rejection or revision does not authorize the proposed application.
A context correction or new learner response may start a new cycle from U/C. Automatic retries and replanning are not assumed in the documented runtime.
failureSemantics: Cyclic plan, unknown agent or unauthorized retrieval: no execution of the invalid plan.
FAILED or SKIPPED dependency: the dependent task is SKIPPED with an explicit cause.
Retrieval error: do not pretend sources were retrieved. If necessary for the task, the step fails; an alternative without search requires a new admissibility evaluation.
Nonempty plan with all steps failed or skipped: orchestration failure; understandable message without sensitive details.
At least one successful step permits the documented synthesis, but the response is partial if required results are missing. The Lead does not arbitrarily fill failed portions.
An empty plan is allowed for clarification, limitations, status or synthesis of already available results. It is not a way to bypass specialist delegation required for teaching.

Worker output formally received but semantically nonconforming: content excluded from the response and updates until corrected. This semantic gate is a final workflow requirement, not behavior demonstrated by the PUML files.

normativeRules.requirement: The metamodel is fixed. Subject models and state may vary within policy limits; no proposal may change types, categories or invariants during execution. A DRAFT/PREPARATION context may precede the first model, provided identity and policy come from trusted configuration. A LEARNING/ACTIVE context cannot have empty models.
normativeRules.onViolation: Reject the contract change and describe the limitation.

normativeRules.requirement: Every entity has an id, version and provenance. Every reference resolves an object of the expected type and exact version; session references remain within the authorized context. DomainModel.definitions may reference only domain_configuration definitions. Loading follows the relevant reference closure, including historical versions needed for evidence and decisions.
normativeRules.onViolation: Block uses depending on the invalid reference; do not resolve by name similarity.

normativeRules.requirement: Topics, classifications, scales, contexts and strategies are model data. Human roles, worker roles and control components remain distinct.
normativeRules.onViolation: Correct the mapping without adding agent categories or fixed subject taxonomies.

normativeRules.requirement: The parentTopics relationship has no cycles. Associative relationships may be cyclic and do not imply prerequisites.
normativeRules.onViolation: Report the hierarchical cycle; do not indiscriminately prohibit semantic cycles between packages or references.

normativeRules.requirement: A MANDATORY prerequisite must be SATISFIED according to a defined rule before the dependent activity. UNKNOWN does not count as SATISFIED. RECOMMENDED and RECOMMENDED_SEQUENCE produce findings; CO_REQUISITE requires a joint satisfaction policy. Obligation cycles that prevent starting are invalid.
normativeRules.onViolation: Block the dependent task and propose prerequisite review or diagnosis; do not block a diagnosis that does not depend on the outcome not yet acquired.

normativeRules.requirement: LearningDesign.root is a PHASE. A ready PHASE contains at least one child and no direct activities; a ready UNIT contains at least one activity and no children. The hierarchy is acyclic, with one parent per node in the path. Composition and completion conditions are explicit before automatic advancement. Node closure uses the relevant ActivityOccurrence states and its rule; COMPLETED does not prove acquisition and SKIPPED does not count as completion unless an explicit authorized rule says so. A finished WorkerTask instance does not automatically complete the learner's activity.
normativeRules.onViolation: Allow a declared draft; prevent undetermined advancement. Reusable activities remain references, not multiple containments.

normativeRules.requirement: A ready path covers its outcomes through unit activities. Each assessment covers the outcomes it declares it evaluates. A task covers its goal or declares the missing portion.
normativeRules.onViolation: Report uncovered outcomes; do not confuse presence in the catalog with path membership or actual coverage.

normativeRules.requirement: In LEARNING, a resource used must have a valid, approved binding consistent with the context, audience and task. PREPARATION allows candidates within the authorized scope. A mandatory requirement must be satisfied before the activity. Discovering resources outside scope is possible only in a separate authorized PREPARATION context, not as an implicit exception to the LEARNING filter.
normativeRules.onViolation: Block access or the affected task; propose alternative material without automatically approving it.

normativeRules.requirement: Distinguish source, usage conditions, derived material, citation and claim. Generated resources declare their origin and sources actually used. A search score does not confer reliability or approval.
normativeRules.onViolation: Remove unverifiable citations and unsupported claims, or qualify them as assumptions or proposals.

normativeRules.requirement: Criterion keys are unique within the rubric and level keys within the criterion. Every CriterionJudgment references existing keys in the applied version and relevant evidence. Weights and aggregation are required only when specified by the rule.
normativeRules.onViolation: No aggregated score or formal judgment while the required rubric is incomplete.

normativeRules.requirement: Actual evidence references the person, context, activity, occurrence/attempt, outcomes and versions. Its type must be allowed by the assessment specification. Agent-produced text and technical task success are not themselves proof of learning. The evidence's person, context and activity references must agree with the indicated ActivityOccurrence. Its historical version identifies the attempt even if the occurrence state evolves.
normativeRules.onViolation: Reject the unsupported assessment link; optionally preserve the event as an interaction without attributing competence.

normativeRules.requirement: Acquisition or a determined judgment requires defined rules and sufficient inputs. An ambiguous or free-form source description does not automatically become an executable predicate. Missing evidence or criteria produces UNKNOWN/undetermined.
normativeRules.onViolation: Provide descriptive feedback or a proposed criterion; do not invent thresholds, levels, weights or success.

normativeRules.requirement: VERIFIED requires ACQUIRED according to criteria, admissible evidence, a satisfied verificationRule, formal evaluation and confirmation by an authorized human. ACQUIRED may be recorded with an approved rule and existing authorization without equating to verification.
normativeRules.onViolation: Maintain UNVERIFIED or PENDING_CONFIRMATION; do not issue implicit certifications.

normativeRules.requirement: Required task capabilities ⊆ capabilities authorized by profile and context. Capabilities actually exposed to the worker ⊆ required capabilities. Tools, APIs, KBs and data follow the same scope constraint.
normativeRules.onViolation: Choose an already configured minimal profile or block delegation; the prompt does not replace enforcement.

normativeRules.requirement: Authorization for mediated retrieval does not automatically expose a tool to the worker. No worker inherits rights from the Lead, previous tasks or retrieved sources; reads are limited to necessary context.
normativeRules.onViolation: Remove excess access and content before delegating; if impossible, do not execute.

normativeRules.requirement: Each specialization has one category and one role from the closed taxonomy. Task intent, output and topic are consistent with that profile. The Socratic constraint permits neither direct nor indirectly revealed solutions, including in synthesis.
normativeRules.onViolation: Separate mixed intents into appropriate tasks; reject or correct outputs violating the contract.

normativeRules.requirement: Steps have unique IDs, existing agents and dependencies within the same plan, without self-dependencies or cycles. Application control verifies limits and permissions and applies stable sequential topological ordering.
normativeRules.onViolation: Reject the invalid plan before calling retrieval or TaskTool.

normativeRules.requirement: An unsuccessful dependency prevents the dependent step. A nonempty plan with no successes ends in error. Synthesis uses only usable outputs and explicitly declares partial coverage. SUCCEEDED in the final workflow also requires per-step semantic review; completion of the call alone is insufficient. The check occurs before output may become input to a dependent task.
normativeRules.onViolation: Do not turn failures, skips or rejected content into successful results.

normativeRules.requirement: A conforming proposal remains a proposal until the required decision. Only an authorized responsible person may approve it; approval and application are distinct events. A revision request entails a new version to review. The decision references the version actually reviewed and its reviewedPayloadKey. A new revision adding only status or a decision link retains approval if substantive content is unchanged. Application control verifies content identity without trusting a key declared by the agent. A ChangeProposal decision may also approve bindings or evaluations included in the candidate: their reviewPayloadKey must appear in coveredPayloadKeys and be part of the content actually reviewed. An object added or modified after review does not inherit proposal approval.
normativeRules.onViolation: Leave the proposal pending, rejected or requiring revision without applying it.

normativeRules.requirement: Apply a change only if authorization, base versions, references and constraints remain valid. Record the cause, author/controller, decision or policy, previous revision and next revision. Do not reinterpret historical evidence with a new rubric. Audit events alone or administrative proposal updates do not change the revision of the authoritative state on which it is based. Substantive changes to that context instead require a base check. The history of an approved evaluation or binding remains reconstructable after later administrative revisions.
normativeRules.onViolation: Mark the proposal STALE if the revision is incompatible; revalidate and, if the approved object changes, require a new decision.

normativeRules.requirement: The response distinguishes grounded content, explicit inference, gaps and proposals. It reports sources actually used when content is source-based; preserves the educational role and does not claim unapplied updates.
normativeRules.onViolation: Correct the synthesis or provide a partial outcome/clarification; no fictitious response to conceal an error.

workerMinimum: content consistent with role and goal
sources used and provenance of generated material
finalResponseMinimum: content useful to the user in the chosen teaching mode
status of any updates: proposed, approved, applied or not applied
outputContract.implementationBoundary: These are semantic contracts. The PUML files document worker outputs and the final response as text; they are not assumed to already be structured records or validated against these fields.

compatibilityMap.documented: The Lead produces ExecutionPlan and synthesis; the Orchestrator validates and executes.
compatibilityMap.boundary: No tools added to the Lead.

compatibilityMap.documented: ExecutionPlan.steps; PlanStep.id, agent, task, depends_on, retrieval.
compatibilityMap.metamodel: TaskPlan.tasks → steps; WorkerTask.stepKey → id; specialization.registryName → agent; brief → task; dependsOn.stepKey → depends_on; retrievalNeed → retrieval when authorized.
compatibilityMap.boundary: Pedagogical references and expected outputs supplement the briefing or a controlled context; they are not new fields already supported by PlanStep. Before dispatch, control resolves references and builds the authorized briefing; task text is not a way to introduce instructions or access exceeding permissions.

compatibilityMap.documented: tool=search_documents, query and k between 1 and 20; search before the worker.
compatibilityMap.metamodel: The information need becomes a concrete request only after permission checks.
compatibilityMap.boundary: 1..20 is a documented adapter limit, not a universal pedagogical rule. Filtering for approved bindings is not shown in the PUML files and is an additional requirement. Document.id/metadata must allow verifiable association with the allowed Resource and binding/version; without that mapping, the result is not presented as an approved source.

compatibilityMap.documented: AgentConfig: name, description, model, tools, skills, system_prompt, source; only name/description for the Lead.
compatibilityMap.metamodel: AgentSpecialization describes category, role and scope associated with existing configurations.
compatibilityMap.boundary: No fields are implicitly added to AgentConfig. Semantic classification and its verification must be provided by the system; selection remains constrained to the actual registry.

compatibilityMap.documented: The worker is created using the configuration's skills/tools.
compatibilityMap.metamodel: R14 and R15 require access strictly necessary for the individual task.
compatibilityMap.boundary: Compatibility is achieved with already minimal profiles; dynamic tool filtering is not demonstrated. If both are missing, the requirement is not satisfied.

compatibilityMap.documented: New worker per step; stable topological ordering; sequential execution.
compatibilityMap.metamodel: WorkerTask and TaskResult, explicit context for every delegation.
compatibilityMap.boundary: No autonomous worker memory, concurrent execution or Architect/Builder pair internal to workers.

compatibilityMap.documented: Skip on unsuccessful dependency; error if all steps fail/skip; synthesis with an empty plan or at least one success.
compatibilityMap.boundary: The source does not specify all error details. In the PUML files, worker return is marked success; per-step semantic validation before output reuse in dependencies is an added requirement. It cannot be deferred solely to final synthesis.

compatibilityMap.documented: Configuration loading and plan validation are shown; a pedagogical model repository with version resolution is not.
compatibilityMap.metamodel: workflow C/V; EntityRef; DomainModel; coverage and readiness rules.
compatibilityMap.boundary: Final workflow contract to be supported by application control without attributing its existence to current code.

compatibilityMap.documented: The MAS runtime shows step statuses; learning persistence and human decisions are absent from the PUML files. Helper and the note propose them for the source runtime.
compatibilityMap.metamodel: ExecutionContext, LearningState, ChangeProposal, HumanDecision and StateChange.
compatibilityMap.boundary: Conceptual definitions required for the requested workflow, not existing implementations.

compatibilityMap.documented: The megamodel contains blueprints, evidence types and rubricKey; complete rubrics and operational rules are missing.
compatibilityMap.metamodel: AssessmentSpecification, Rubric, RuleDefinition, Evaluation and Citation.
compatibilityMap.boundary: The schema establishes what data is needed. Thresholds, specific criteria, answer keys and content remain variable models.

compatibilityMap.documented: An answer(question) call produces a plan, executes steps and synthesizes.
compatibilityMap.metamodel: New turns may restart from an updated context.
compatibilityMap.boundary: No executable branching, retries or automatic replanning is attributed to the existing plan.

traceability.sourceConcept: Four major categories and specialization before use
traceability.treatment: Current requirement, closed taxonomy with five roles in four categories.

traceability.sourceConcept: Lead without tools, Python control, TaskTool, registry, worker per step and mediated retrieval
traceability.treatment: Preserved boundaries; no transfer of agent powers described in the source note.

traceability.sourceConcept: Competencies::Competency, Certification Design::CompetencyCluster, Prerequisite and Domain
traceability.treatment: AIM-PRO-specific categories removed; topic distinguished from expected outcome; prerequisite satisfaction formalized as a requirement.

traceability.sourceConcept: Scenario::Scenario, APhase, Phase, PhaseGroup, Module and Goal
traceability.treatment: Phase/group unified in the composite node; goals expressed as references to outcomes. Recursion preserved; ordering and completion made explicit. Pedagogical parallelism abstracted as independence compatible with sequential tasks.

traceability.sourceConcept: iSQD: five families and 25 concrete strategies
traceability.treatment: Specific class hierarchy removed; strategies become selectable data, not a mandatory sequence or worker categories.
Instructions, outcomes, form and evidence preserved; exposition and dialogue added to cover Teacher and Socratic. No abstract instance or incomplete item is copied.

traceability.sourceConcept: Resources::Resource, OER, GeneratedOER and proposed ResourceBinding
traceability.treatment: Need, candidate, source, derived material, usage conditions and approved selection separated. Resource/activity relationship 0..* rather than 1..*: external resources mandatory only when required, allowing independent dialogues without fictitious citations.
Reusable blueprint and local assessment unified; rubrics and rules are necessary formalizations, not reconstructions of an unattached Offering schema.

traceability.sourceConcept: Offering, participants, evidence, acquired/verified and accountable decisions
traceability.treatment: Delivery generalized as session/context. The path is optional for isolated requests; versions and evidence remain mandatory where needed.

traceability.sourceConcept: Proposal → control → approval → application; six value origins
traceability.treatment: Application separated from decision. Ordinary events recordable under policy; formal verifications and authoritative changes retain human control.

traceability.sourceConcept: Duplicate Users::iSQD_Profile and Scenario::iSQD_Profile profiles; Educators; platform metadata
traceability.treatment: Profiles consolidated; empty classes, digital twins, internal URIs, errors and unused enumerations removed. Human Teacher role not confused with TEACHER agent.

traceability.sourceConcept: Complete workflow required beyond a text response alone
traceability.treatment: Validation added before planning and plan validation retained after production. Persistent state, approvals and resource filtering declared as requirements not demonstrated.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: Request for an explanation of a known topic; a minimal Teacher profile and relevant approved material exist.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: Teacher plan, retrieval only if useful and authorized, explanation with sources used; no acquisition or verification attributed merely for listening.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: Mixed request for a lesson, practice and assessment.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: Distinct Teacher, Trainer and Evaluator tasks with dependencies only where necessary. The test may be generated now; evaluation awaits the user's actual responses.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: Socratic guidance on the same problem for which a previous output contains the solution.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: The solution is neither shown nor disguised as a hint. Limited question or suggestion; wait for the user's reasoning. The Lead preserves the constraint.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: A mandatory prerequisite is missing or unknown.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: The dependent activity does not start; prerequisite review or diagnosis is possible. A nonmandatory recommendation produces only a finding.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: A resource is missing in LEARNING. A Curator in a separate authorized PREPARATION context finds a candidate not yet bound to the learning session.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: The tutor neither uses nor retrieves the unapproved candidate. A resource proposal originates in PREPARATION; a binding is proposed and approved for LEARNING, then application control applies it. No automatic transfer of data or permissions between contexts.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: The existing profile has excess tools and the runtime cannot limit them by task.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: No delegation to that profile; choose a suitable minimal profile or report the gap. Writing “do not use” in the prompt does not satisfy the requirement.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: Quiz received and response available, but required threshold or rubric undefined.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: Descriptive feedback or proposed criteria; no invented formal outcome, acquisition or verification.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: Plan with a nonexistent dependency reference or cycle.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: Rejection before any retrieval or delegation.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: A step fails, its dependent is skipped and an independent task succeeds.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: Synthesis of successful portions only, explicit gaps and no updates based on the failed portion. If none succeeds, orchestration failure.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: An approved proposal references a state revision that is now incompatible.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: No application; STALE proposal, revalidation and a new decision if the content subject to approval changes.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: Two sessions share the same model; the learner completes an activity in only one.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: Evidence and state updated only in the owning context. Every reuse preserves occurrence, attempt and version.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: Isolated request without a complete path, schedule or previously modeled activity.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: Clarify or propose the minimum definition of the activity and required outcomes. No mandatory artificial course. An ordinary explanation may be delivered; recording it as assessment evidence requires the necessary references.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: Structurally valid model but a unit declared ready without activities or covered outcomes.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: Draft not ready, with completeness findings; do not present it as an executable path.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: A specialization absent from the registry is required.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: Explicit gap; no invented name in PlanStep.agent. Semantic refinement allowed only for an already suitable, authorized profile.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: Positive formal evaluation by the Evaluator without confirmation from the responsible human.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: Acquisition only if already authorized by a rule; verification remains pending or unverified. The agent is not the human decision-maker.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: Pedagogically independent phase with two activities both necessary for completion.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: Activities schedulable without mutual pedagogical order; tasks still executed one at a time. The phase does not close before its declared completion condition.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: An output is technically returned by the worker but violates the contract, before a dependent task.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: Immediate check before reuse: TaskResult FAILED; dependent task SKIPPED. No rejected content reaches its briefing.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: A decision approves a proposal version; the next revision adds only APPROVED status and the decision link.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: The decision remains valid for the same verified reviewPayloadKey. Changing the proposal's effect instead requires a new content identity and a new decision.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: First request for a subject without a DomainModel, with valid initial identities and PolicySet.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: DRAFT/PREPARATION with empty models; candidate model proposal linked to the base context; validation and decision before activation. Without initial permissions, request configuration and do not delegate.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: A new domain uses its own subject taxonomy and calls the responsible human a teacher.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: The taxonomy is modeled as data without changing classes or categories. The human teacher is not mistaken for the TEACHER worker and their permissions are not transferred to it.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: Two topics reference each other as related topics; another set proposes a cyclic parentTopics hierarchy.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: Reciprocal associative relationships are allowed; the hierarchical cycle is rejected. Neither relationship is implicitly converted into a prerequisite or task dependency.

acceptanceScenarios.situation: A resource has a high retrieval score but does not support a sentence in the synthesis; a summary was generated from multiple materials.
acceptanceScenarios.expected: The sentence receives neither a fictitious citation nor reliability derived from the score. The summary declares its generated origin and materials actually used; usage conditions and approval are verified separately.

acceptanceScenarioStatus: Specification acceptance cases, not tests executed on the runtime. Checks on this file concern syntax, internal references, requirement coverage and document review.

intentionallyVariable: resource policies, permissions and responsible people
nonGoalsAndOpenValues.minimalEnablement: Relevant models, a suitable profile, permissions and necessary data are sufficient for a task. Recording evidence, evaluating or updating verified state also requires the specified definitions and decisions. Gaps are not filled by modifying the metamodel.

designDecisions.choice: A single declarative, readable JSON with typed references.
designDecisions.reason: Maintains a single specification analogous in function to the megamodel, without pretending to be an importable format or implementation.

designDecisions.choice: Semantic review before every output reuse, in addition to synthesis checks.
designDecisions.reason: Prevents propagation of disallowed sources, prohibited solutions or nonconforming results.
designDecisions.origin: Clarification of the control requirement; capability not demonstrated in the PUML files.

designDecisions.choice: Approval of substantive content with a stable identity, separate from administrative revisions.
designDecisions.reason: Prevents recording a decision from immediately invalidating that same decision.
designDecisions.origin: New formalization of proposal, decision and application.

designDecisions.choice: Separate preparation context for discovering new materials.
designDecisions.reason: Preserves the scope of approved tutoring materials without implicit exceptions.
designDecisions.origin: Integration of the two scopes described by helper.

designDecisions.choice: Trusted bootstrap and DRAFT context without models, with isolated candidate proposals.
designDecisions.reason: Allows preparation of a new domain without pretending configuration is ready or granting permissions to the Lead.
designDecisions.origin: New formalization, not functionality demonstrated in the runtime.

designDecisions.choice: Activity occurrence separate from the definition and worker task.
designDecisions.reason: Enables reuse, attempts and observable progress without confusing learning with technical completion.
designDecisions.origin: Integration of reusable path and runtime state.
